REAL: isKmsi (msal-common dist/account/AuthToken.mjs:32-45) is computed in ResponseHandler.mjs:135 and threaded via CacheManager.saveCacheRecord (dist/cache/CacheManager.mjs:205-222) through BrowserCacheManager.setAccount/set*Credential into LocalStorage.setUserData, which at msal-browser dist/cache/LocalStorage.mjs:116-122 writes the entity PLAINTEXT when kmsi is true; getItemFromEncryptedCache (LocalStorage.mjs:230-234) keeps unencrypted entries on import so KMSI entries survive browser restart despite the session-scoped encryption cookie; AccountInfo.mjs:84 populates kmsi on public account objects. Also, the real implementation spans TokenCache.mjs lines 31-69 (helpers through 174), not 31-71 as cited; minor line-range imprecision only.

confirmed.title: authenticationScheme "pop"/"ssh" (PoP token binding) entirely missing — requests silently downgraded to Bearer
confirmed.realBehavior: With request.authenticationScheme: "pop", real generates an ECDSA keypair, sends token_type=pop and req_cnf (base64url {kid, xms_ksl:"sw"}) in the token-endpoint body on both auth-code and refresh-token grants, caches the AT under credentialType AccessToken_With_AuthScheme with keyId and tokenType "pop" (different cache key), returns result.tokenType "pop", and returns result.accessToken as a signed SHR JWT — re-signed even on cache hits (throws keyIdMissing if the cached entity lacks keyId). "ssh" similarly sends token_type=ssh + req_cnf from request.sshJwk. The throttle thumbprint also carries the scheme.
confirmed.realEvidence: node_modules/@azure/msal-common/dist/client/AuthorizationCodeClient.mjs:169-190 and RefreshTokenClient.mjs:196-213 (addPopToken/addSshJwk); request/RequestParameterBuilder.mjs:396-410 (token_type + req_cnf params); crypto/PopTokenGenerator.mjs (generateCnf/signPopToken); response/ResponseHandler.mjs:250-261 (cache-hit SHR re-signing, keyIdMissing) and :317 (result.tokenType from entity); cache/utils/CacheHelpers.mjs:55-82 (ACCESS_TOKEN_WITH_AUTH_SCHEME credentialType + keyId from cnf.kid)

Token requests never carry token_type/req_cnf, the AT is always cached as credentialType "AccessToken" with tokenType "Bearer", result.tokenType is hardcoded "Bearer" on network and cache-hit paths, the access token is returned raw, and the throttle key hardcodes authenticationScheme "Bearer".

The IdP never receives req_cnf/token_type, and a storage dump shows a Bearer AccessToken entity instead of an AccessToken_With_AuthScheme entity with keyId.

verdict.reason: REAL: verified in dist. msal-common/dist/client/AuthorizationCodeClient.mjs (~line 169) and RefreshTokenClient.mjs (~line 196) both branch on request.authenticationScheme === POP, calling PopTokenGenerator.generateCnf and addPopToken; RequestParameterBuilder.mjs addPopToken/addSshJwk set token_type=pop|ssh and req_cnf in the token-endpoint body; SSH without sshJwk throws missingSshJwk. ResponseHandler.mjs generateAuthenticationResult re-signs the cached secret via signPopToken on cache hits when entity tokenType is pop (throws keyIdMissing if keyId absent) and returns result.tokenType from the cached entity. CacheHelpers.mjs createAccessTokenEntity switches credentialType to ACCESS_TOKEN_WITH_AUTH_SCHEME for non-Bearer tokenType and sets keyId from the AT's cnf.kid claim. This is live browser-path code: msal-browser/dist/request/RequestHelpers.mjs defaults authenticationScheme to Bearer and validates PoP requests, so the scheme flows through standard acquireToken* calls. MINI: packages/browser/src/index.ts TokenRequest (lines 72-93) has no authenticationScheme field; throttle key (line 938), cached AT entity (line 1045: credentialType "AccessToken", tokenType "Bearer"), network result (line 1093) and cache-hit result (line 1338) all hardcode "Bearer"; no req_cnf/token_type is ever sent (token body/query built without them); no PoP code exists in compat/src or react/src. OBSERVABLE: the IdP sees missing token_type/req_cnf body params, the app sees result.tokenType "Bearer" and a raw (non-SHR) accessToken that a PoP-protected resource rejects, and a storage dump shows credentialType "AccessToken" without keyId instead of "AccessToken_With_AuthScheme". UNCOVERED: grep of test/conformance/scenarios/*.mjs finds authenticationScheme only in 10-naa.mjs, where the NAA bridge mock echoes the default Bearer scheme; no scenario requests pop/ssh or inspects req_cnf/token_type/SHR signing.
verdict.corrections: Two refinements: (1) Real does not unconditionally generate a fresh ECDSA keypair — if request.popKid is set, it reuses that key (cryptoUtils.encodeKid) and the cache-hit path skips SHR re-signing (returns the raw secret). The keypair-generation description applies to the common no-popKid case. (2) "The property is silently ignored" is accurate for mini's core web token flows, but mini's feature modules do forward authenticationScheme through bridge transports: packages/browser/src/naa.ts:251 (tokenType: naaReq.authenticationScheme) and packages/browser/src/broker.ts:305-307 (forwards rest.authenticationScheme as tokenType to the platform broker). The gap as stated — no PoP/SSH support in the token-endpoint acquisition path (auth-code + refresh-token grants), caching, or result shaping — stands.

confirmed.title: No knownAuthorities/untrusted-authority validation or AAD instance discovery — mini trusts any authority in default protocolMode

verdict.corrections: Two factual corrections: (1) A "no match" in a successful instance-discovery response does NOT reject — Authority.mjs:638-643 treats it as the trusted custom-domain scenario and synthesizes cloud discovery metadata from the host (createCloudDiscoveryMetadataFromHost). Only an invalid_instance error response, a malformed (non-CloudInstanceDiscovery) response body, or a network error return null from getCloudDiscoveryMetadataFromNetwork and yield untrusted_authority. The suggestedTest remains valid since it blocks/stubs the discovery request (network error path). (2) Mini's Config type does not "accept" protocolMode/knownAuthorities/cloudDiscoveryMetadata — the keys are absent from the interface entirely (index.ts:95-129), so TypeScript consumers get excess-property errors while JS consumers are silently ignored; the sole occurrence of cloudDiscoveryMetadata in mini is an empty-string default in the getConfiguration() output snapshot at index.ts:1524, not a config input.

verdict.corrections: Minor corrections: (1) The cited react dist is @azure/msal-react v5.5.1 (paired with msal-browser 5.16), not msal-browser itself. (2) Real useIsAuthenticated returns false during startup via an explicit InteractionStatus.Startup guard in the hook, not (only) because provider accounts start empty. (3) In TypeScript, mini's parameterless useIsAuthenticated(matchAccount) is a compile error rather than a silent degradation; the silent wrong-answer degradation applies to plain-JS consumers or type-erased call sites. (4) Mini's AuthenticatedTemplate/UnauthenticatedTemplate do guard inProgress==="startup", so the startup flash affects direct useIsAuthenticated() callers, not the template components. (5) The claimed real iat/nonce re-render behavior is accurate but mini does not observably diverge on that specific point: the mini provider's JSON.stringify comparison of accounts (index.tsx:57) includes idTokenClaims, so changed iat/nonce also propagates a new account object; the confirmed divergences are the missing matchAccount parameter, startup behavior, case-sensitive homeAccountId/localAccountId matching, and the empty-filter-object fallback.
